fields.value: Strongest feature: Price answers why late writers would invoke Paul by proposing that a preexisting Paul–Simon figure, reinforced through polemical and Gnostic reception, supplied authority, while candidly calling the proposal speculative rather than established history. Principal limitation: The proposed identity remains thinly supported because the chronology, patristic testimony, Justin’s silence, and relationships among Pauline, Simonian, Marcionite, and Gnostic traditions are compressed and contested, so the parallels do not demonstrate that this persona existed before the letters. Live burden: Establish a dated chain of independent evidence connecting these figures and communities, then show that this reconstruction explains Pauline authority better than conventional historical-Paul accounts under comparable standards. Locked score: The 69 reflects a responsive, carefully qualified possibility whose calibration cannot overcome its unresolved chronology, uncertain identity link, and limited historical warrant.

Strongest feature: White makes the manuscript tradition a historical test, arguing that branching transmission and tenacious variant readings should preserve traces of a major interpolation, while surviving witnesses contain no manuscript stream without First Corinthians 15:3–11. Principal limitation: The inference assumes branching preceded the alteration, because an insertion made before recoverable streams diverged could pass unanimously into later witnesses and leave exactly the uniform record White cites, despite not belonging to the earliest text. Live burden: Date the relevant branch points and compare expected survival of passage-free witnesses under early-insertion, late-insertion, and original-text models, applying equivalent preservation assumptions throughout. Locked score: The 86 recognizes a clear, highly responsive argument grounded in observed manuscript behavior, but stops higher because absent variants constrain later interpolation without independently excluding alteration before recoverable branching.
